**Allah's words: ﴿He multiplies you through it﴾**

The meaning is that Allah, glory be to Him, makes you live (or multiplies you) through what He created for you of the livestock mentioned.

Al-Kalbi said: "He increases you in this pairing. Without this pairing, offspring would not multiply." The meaning is that He creates you in this manner, which He mentioned, by making for you spouses, for the cause of our creation and the creation of animals is by means of pairs.

The pronoun in His words ﴿through it﴾ refers to the making (ja'l). The meaning of *dhar'* (multiplication) is creation, and here it means abundant creation. It is both creation and multiplication. It was said that *fi* (in) carries the meaning of *ba'* (by), i.e., "He multiplies you by that." This is the view of the Kufans.

The correct view is that it retains its own sense, and the verb includes the meaning of *yunshi'ukum* (He brings you into being), which takes *fi*, as Allah says: ﴿And We bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 61].

**(Benefit)**

The Imam, the Proof of Islam, Abu Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Shafi'i, known as Ibn al-Haddad, may God have mercy on him, said:

The comprehensive formula in the chapter on *tawhid* (the oneness of Allah) is to say: affirmation without likening (*tashbih*), and negation without denial (*ta'til*). Allah says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 11].

The comprehensive formula regarding the ambiguous (*mutashabih*) verses about the attributes is to say: "I believe in what Allah has said, according to what He intended, and I believe in what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, has said, according to what he intended." This is our belief, which we hold to and which we rely upon. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to cause us to live upon it and to cause us to die upon it, and to make it our means on the Day of standing before Him. Truly, He is Generous and Noble. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

**(Section)**

Al-Khallal said: Ali ibn Isa informed me that Hanbal narrated to them, saying: I asked Abu Abd Allah (Ahmad ibn Hanbal) about the narrations that are reported that Allah, glory be to Him, descends to the lowest heaven, that Allah will be seen, that Allah places His foot, and similar narrations. Abu Abd Allah said: "We believe in them and we affirm them... and we do not reject any of them, and we know that what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, brought is true, when they are with sound chains of narration. We do not reject the words of Allah, nor do we describe Him with more than He described Himself, without limit or end: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 11]."

And Hanbal said in another place, from Ahmad: "There is nothing like unto Him in His essence, as He described Himself. Allah, blessed and exalted, has described Himself in a general way, so He set for Himself an attribute to which nothing is similar. His attributes are not limited or known except by what He described Himself with. Allah said: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 11]. He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing without limit or measure. Those who describe Him cannot reach His description. We do not go beyond the Qur'an and the Hadith, so we say as He said, and we describe Him with what He described Himself with, and we do not go beyond that, and those who describe Him cannot reach His attributes. We believe in the whole Qur'an, its clear (*muhkam*) and its ambiguous (*mutashabih*), and we do not remove from Him any of His attributes because of a shameful accusation that has been leveled. And what He described Himself with of speech, descent, privacy with His servant on the Day of Resurrection, and placing His palm upon him: all of this indicates that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, will be seen in the Hereafter. Limiting this in any way is an innovation (*bid'ah*), and submitting to it for Allah is without attribute or limit, except what He described Himself with: All-Hearing, All-Seeing; He has never ceased to be Speaking, Knowing, Forgiving, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Knower of hidden things. These are attributes with which He described Himself, which cannot be repelled or rejected, and He is above the Throne without limit, as Allah said: ﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], however He willed. The will is to Him, and the power is to Him. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Creator of all things, and He, as He described Himself, is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, without limit or measure. We do not go beyond the Qur'an and the Hadith..."

...exalted above what the Jahmiyyah (followers of Jahm ibn Safwan) and the Mushabbihah (anthropomorphists) say. I said to him: "And what do you say the anthropomorphist (*mushabbih*) is?" He said: "Whoever says: 'His sight is like my sight, His hand is like my hand, His foot is like my foot,' has likened Allah, glory be to Him, to His creation."

**(Section)**

The words of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾

He intended by it only the negation that there should be a partner with Him, or a deity deserving worship and exaltation, as the anthropomorphists and polytheists do.

He did not intend by it the negation of His attributes of perfection, His elevation above His creation, His speaking through His books, His speaking to His messengers, or the believers' seeing Him clearly with their eyes, as one sees the sun and the moon on a clear day.

For He, glory be to Him, mentioned this only in the context of His refutation of the polytheists who took protectors other than Him, whom they befriended besides Him. So He said: ﴿Those who take protectors besides Him, Allah is Watchful over them, and you are not a guardian over them. And thus We revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an, that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt: a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze. Had Allah willed, He would have made them one community, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers have no protector nor helper. Or have they taken protectors besides Him? But Allah is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things Powerful. Whatever you differ over, its judgment is with Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; in Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn repentantly. Originator of the heavens and the earth; He has made for you from yourselves mates, and among the livestock mates; He multiplies you through it. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 6-11].

So reflect on how He mentioned this negation as an establishment of *tawhid*, and as a nullification of what the people of polytheism held: the likening of their gods and their protectors to Him, to the point that they worshipped them alongside Him. The distorters distorted it and made it a shield for themselves in negating the attributes of His perfection and the realities of His names and actions.

This likening that Allah nullified, in negation and prohibition, is the root of the polytheism of the world and the worship of idols. For this reason the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade that anyone prostrate to a creature like himself, or swear by a creature like himself, or pray toward a grave, or take it as a mosque, or hang a lamp upon it, or say: "What Allah wills and what so-and-so wills," and the like, out of caution against this likening which is the root of polytheism.

As for affirming the attributes of perfection, that is the root of *tawhid*.

Thus it becomes clear that the *mushabbihah* are those who liken the created to the Creator in worship, exaltation, humility, swearing by him, vowing to him, prostrating to him, devoting oneself at his house, shaving the head for him, seeking aid from him, and associating him with Allah, as in saying: "I have none but Allah and you," "I rely on Allah and on you," "This is from Allah and from you," "I am under the protection of Allah and yours," "What Allah wills and what you will," "This is for Allah and for you."

And similar things.

These are truly the *mushabbihah*, not the people of *tawhid*, who affirm for Allah what He affirmed for Himself, and negate from Him what He negated from Himself, who do not make for Him a rival from His creation, nor an equal, nor a peer, nor a namesake, and for whom there is no protector or intercessor besides Him.

Whoever reflects upon this section with true reflection will see how the trial came upon the earth through the worship of idols, and will see the secret of the Qur'an in its denunciation of these *mushabbihah* who likened, especially when they combine with this likening the *ta'til* (negation) of the attributes and actions, as is most common among them.

So they combine the negation of the Lord, glory be to Him, from His attributes of perfection with the likening of His creation to Him.

**(Section)**

The words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾

For He, glory be to Him, mentioned this after mentioning the qualities of His perfection and His descriptions. So He said: ﴿Ha Mim. 'Ayn Sin Qaf. Thus Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, reveals to you and to those before you. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Most High, the Mighty. The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them, and the angels exalt the praise of their Lord and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful. And those who take protectors besides Him, Allah is Watchful over them, and you are not a guardian over them﴾ [ash-Shura: 1-6].

Up to His words: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth; He has made for you from yourselves mates, and among the livestock mates; He multiplies you through it. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 11].

So this One described by these attributes, qualities, actions, loftiness, greatness, protection, might, wisdom, sovereignty, praise, forgiveness, mercy, speech, will, guardianship, giving life to the dead, complete and all-encompassing power, judging among His servants, and being the Originator of the heavens and the earth, and He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing: this is the One for whom there is nothing like Him, because of the abundance of His qualities, attributes, names, and actions, and their affirmation for Him in the manner of perfection, in which nothing resembles Him. So the one who affirms the attributes, loftiness, speech, actions, and realities of the names is the One whom He, glory be to Him, describes as having nothing like Him.

As for the *mu'attil* (the negator) who denies His attributes and the realities of His names, his description of Him as having nothing like Him is metaphorical, not literal, as he says of all His other attributes and names.

For this reason some of the early scholars said: the negators combined likening and negation. They called their negation "transcendence" (*tanzih*), and they called what He described Himself with "likening" (*tashbih*). They made what indicates the affirmation of the attributes of perfection and their abundance a proof of their negation and suspension. This passed over those whom Allah had not given light, and was deceived by it whoever Allah willed; but Allah guides whoever holds fast to revelation, reason, and natural disposition (*fitrah*). And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

**(Section)**

Among the most noble kinds of knowledge is the knowledge of the Lord, glory be to Him, through beauty. It is the knowledge of the elite of creation, and all of them know Him through one of His attributes, and the most complete knowledge is that of one who knows Him through His perfection, majesty, and beauty, glory be to Him: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ in all His attributes. Even if you supposed all creation to be upon the most beautiful form, and all of them upon that form, and you attributed their outward and inward beauty to the beauty of the Lord, glory be to Him, it would be less than the ratio of a weak lamp to the disc of the sun. It suffices for His beauty that if the veil were lifted from His face, His glories would burn up everything that His sight reached of His creation. It suffices for His beauty that every beauty, outward and inward, in this world and the Hereafter, is among the traces of His craftsmanship; so what then is the assumption about the One from whom this beauty proceeds? It suffices for His beauty that to Him belongs all might, all power, all generosity, all benevolence, all knowledge, and all grace. And by the light of His face the darknesses were illuminated, as the Prophet said in the supplication at al-Ta'if:

"I seek refuge in the light of Your face, by which the darknesses are illuminated, and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right."

And Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "With your Lord there is no night or day. The light of the heavens and the earth is from the light of His face. He, glory be to Him, is the light of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day of Resurrection, when He comes to judge, the earth will shine with His light."

Among His most beautiful names is *al-Jamil* (the Beautiful). And in the authentic (*Sahih*) hadith from him: "Truly Allah is beautiful and loves beauty." His beauty, glory be to Him, is of four degrees: the beauty of His Essence, the beauty of His attributes, the beauty of His actions, and the beauty of His names. His names are all the most beautiful, His attributes are all attributes of perfection, and His actions are all wisdom, benefit, justice, and mercy. As for the beauty of His Essence and what He is, it is a matter that none other comprehends and none other knows. Creation has of it only the indications by which He made Himself known to whom He honored among His servants. For that beauty is protected from others, veiled by the covering of the cloak and the garment, as His Messenger said, relating from Him: "Greatness is My cloak, and majesty is My garment." And since greatness is greater and more encompassing, it is more worthy of the name "cloak." For He, glory be to Him, is the Great, the Most High, and He is the Exalted, the Mighty. Ibn Abbas said: "He veiled the Essence with the attributes, and veiled the attributes with the actions. So what do you suppose of a beauty veiled by the descriptions of perfection and covered by the attributes of greatness and majesty?"

From this meaning some aspects of the beauty of His Essence can be understood. For the servant ascends from knowledge of the actions to knowledge of the attributes, and from knowledge of the attributes to knowledge of the Essence. When he witnesses something of the beauty of the actions, he infers from it the beauty of the attributes, and then from the beauty of the attributes he infers the beauty of the Essence. From here it becomes clear that all praise belongs to Him, and that none of His creation can count His praises; rather He is as He praised Himself. He deserves to be worshipped for His Essence, to be loved for His Essence, and to be thanked for His Essence. He, glory be to Him, loves Himself, praises Himself, and extols Himself. His love for Himself, His praise of Himself, His extolling of Himself, and His declaring His oneness for Himself are in reality the praise, extolling, love, and oneness. He, glory be to Him, is as He praised Himself and above what His creation praises Him with. And He, glory be to Him, loves His Essence as He loves His attributes and actions. All His actions are good and beloved, even if among what is affected by them there is what He dislikes and hates; there is nothing in His actions that is hateful or displeasing.

There is nothing in existence that is loved for its own sake and praised for its own sake except Him, glory be to Him. Every other thing loved, if its love stems from love of Him, such that it is loved for His sake, then its love is sound; otherwise it is false love. This is the reality of divinity, for the true God is the One who is loved for His own sake and praised for His own sake. How much more so when His benevolence, favor, forbearance, pardon, forgiveness, kindness, and mercy are added to that. The servant must know that there is no god but Allah, so he loves Him and praises Him for His Essence and perfection. And he must know that there is no true benefactor of the various outward and inward blessings except Him, so he loves Him for His benevolence and favor and praises Him for that. Thus he loves Him for both reasons together. Just as there is nothing like unto Him, His love is not like love (of creatures). And love combined with submission is worship (*'ubudiyyah*), for which the creation was made. For it is the ultimate of love with the ultimate of humility, and this is fitting only for Him, glory be to Him. And associating anyone with Him in this is the polytheism (*shirk*) that Allah will not forgive, and will not accept any deed from its doer.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 42, verse 11 (part 2 of 2):

His praise (hamd) comprises two principles: informing others of His praiseworthy attributes and perfection, and loving Him for them. Whoever informs others of another's good qualities without loving him is not a praiser, and whoever loves him without informing others of his good qualities is not a praiser either, until he combines both. He, glorified is He, praises Himself by Himself, and He praises Himself through what He causes to flow upon the tongues of those who praise Him among His angels, prophets, messengers and believing servants. So He is the One who praises Himself by this and by that. Their praise of Him is by His will, His permission and His creation, for it is He who made the praiser a praiser, the Muslim a Muslim, the one who prays a one who prays, and the one who repents a one who repents. From Him blessings began, and to Him they return. So they began with His praise and ended with His praise. It is He who inspired His servant to repent and rejoices at it with the greatest joy, and it is from His grace and bounty. He inspired His servant to obey, helped him to do so, and then rewarded him for it, and this too is from His grace and bounty. He, glorified is He, is independent of everything other than Him in every respect, while everything other than Him is needy of Him in every respect. The servant is in need of Him in his very essence, in the means and in the ends, for whatever does not come through Him does not come to be, and whatever He does not grant does not benefit.

[Section on Expansion (al-Basṭ)]

The author of al-Manazil (Manazil al-Sa'irin) said:

(Chapter on Expansion (al-Basṭ)) Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿He multiplies you through it﴾ [al-Shura: 11].

I say: The connection of this with the indication of the verse is that Allah, glorified is He, gives you life in what He created for you of the livestock mentioned.

Al-Kalbi said: "He multiplies you through this pairing. Were it not for this pairing, offspring would not increase." The meaning is: He creates you in this manner which was mentioned, that He made for you spouses, for the cause of our creation and the creation of living beings is through pairs. The pronoun in His saying "through it" refers to the making (al-ja'l) of pairs. The meaning of dhar' (multiplying) is creation, and here it means abundant creation; so it is creation and multiplication. It was said that "fi" (in) here means "bi" (through), meaning: He multiplies you by that. This is the view of the Kufans (al-Kufiyyun).

The correct view is that it retains its original meaning, and the verb is taken to include the meaning of "yunshi'ukum" (bring you into being), which takes "fi" as its complement, as He said: ﴿and bring you into being in what you do not know﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 61]. This is the explanation of the verse.

Since life is of two kinds, the life of bodies and the life of spirits, and He, glorified is He, is the One who gives life to the hearts and spirits of His friends by His honouring, His kindness and His expansion, this is an increase for them, a multiplication and a propagation. And Allah knows best.

The author of al-Manazil said: Expansion (al-basṭ) is for the servant to release the witnesses of his inner self in the paths of knowledge, and to let fall upon his inner self the cloak of special favour. These are the people of confusion (al-talbis), and they were expanded in the field of expansion after three meanings, each meaning having a group.

He means: expansion is the release of the servant's outward aspects and actions in accordance with the requirements of knowledge, while his inner self is immersed in watchfulness (muraqabah), love and intimacy with Allah. So his beauty is in both his outward and inward aspects. His outward is clothed in beauty through the requirement of knowledge, and his inward is clothed in beauty through love, hope, fear, watchfulness and intimacy. Thus the outward acts are his outer garment, and the inward states are his undergarment. His state does not diminish the outward ruling upon him, nor does his knowledge cut off the flow of his state. Allah, glorified is He, has combined the two beauties, I mean the beauty of the outward and the beauty of the inward, in more than one place in His Book.

Among them is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment; but the clothing of righteousness – that is best﴾ [al-A'raf: 26].

Among them is His saying, the Exalted, about the women of Paradise: ﴿Therein are good and beautiful [women]﴾ [al-Rahman: 70].

So they are beautiful of face and good in character.

Among them is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He will give them radiance and joy﴾ [al-Insan: 11].

So radiance is the beauty of faces, and joy is the beauty of hearts.

Among them is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22–23].

So radiance adorns their outward aspects, and looking beautifies their inward aspects.

Among them is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21].

So the bracelets beautified their outward aspects, and the pure drink purified their inward aspects.

Among them is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the adornment of the stars and as protection from every rebellious devil﴾ [al-Saffat: 6].

So He beautified its outward with the stars and its inward with protection from the devils.

We return to explaining his words.

His saying: "and they are the people of confusion (al-talbis)": meaning, they are those mentioned in the chapter on Contraction (al-qabd), and they are the second group, who were concealed by the garment of confusion from people's eyes, so their realities are not seen.

His saying: "and they were expanded in the field of expansion": meaning, the Truth, glorified is He, expanded them through the tongue of His Messenger, not what the heretic (al-mulhid) supposes to be delightful listening (al-sama' al-shahi), contemplating a pleasing sight, seeing beautiful images, or hearing enchanting instruments.

Indeed, this is a field which Satan has spread out to snatch souls away from the field which the Most Merciful has set up. The field of the Most Merciful that He spread out is the one He set up for His prophets and friends. It is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was upon with his companions and his family, and with the stranger and the close one: breadth of chest, constant cheerfulness, good character, greeting those he met, standing with whoever sought to stop him, joking in truth with the young and the old at times, accepting invitations, and gentleness of manner, so that each of his companions thought he was the most beloved to him. In this field you find nothing but what is obligatory, recommended, or permissible that helps towards these.

His saying: "A group was expanded as a mercy to creation, they expand to them and mingle with them, and so they are illuminated by their light, while the realities are gathered and the secrets are guarded."

Allah made their expansion with the creatures a mercy for them, as He said: ﴿It was by mercy from Allah that you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude and harsh-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 159].

So the Lord, glorified is He, expanded these people among His creation so that the wayfarer may follow their example, the bewildered may be guided by them, the sick may be healed by them, and the light of their guidance, counsel and knowledge may illuminate the darkness of the nature and desire. The wayfarers follow them when they are silent, and benefit from their words when they speak, for their movements and stillness, being by Allah, for Allah and according to the command of Allah, attracted the hearts of the sincere towards them. This light which shone upon people from them is the light of knowledge and recognition.

The scholars are of three kinds: a scholar whose light is illuminated by him and by whom others are illuminated; this one is among the successors of the messengers and the heirs of the prophets. A scholar whose light illuminates himself but not others; if he does not fall short, his benefit is limited to himself, and there is a difference between him and the first. And a scholar who is not illuminated by his own light, nor is he a light to others; his knowledge is a burden upon him, and his expansion towards people is a trial for them, while the expansion of the first is a mercy for them.

His saying: "and the realities are gathered and the secrets are guarded": meaning, they expanded while the realities within their secrets are gathered in their inner selves. So expansion did not scatter their hearts, did not divide their resolves, and did not loosen the knot of their determinations.

His saying: "and their secrets are guarded": meaning, they are hidden and they do not reveal them to those with whom they expand, even though expansion requires familiarity and each of the two intimates knowing the secret of the other. So beware, then beware, of letting the one with whom you are intimate know your secret with Allah. Rather, draw him in and make him yearn, and guard the trust of Allah with you; do not expose it to being reclaimed.

(Fa'idah)

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The prophets are children of 'Allat (paternal half-brothers)."

And in another wording: "They are brothers from different mothers, but their religion is one."

Al-Jawhari said: "Banu al-'Allat are a man's children from several wives. They were so named because the man who married the first wife married another after her, and then the second wife drank a second draught. The second drink is called 'ullal, after nahl (the first drink), and 'allahu yu'alluhu means he gave him a second drink."

Another scholar said: "They were so named because they are the children of co-wives, and 'allat means co-wives. This second explanation is more evident."

As for the reason for the name, a group of scholars, including Qadi 'Iyad and others, said: its meaning is that the prophets differ in their times, and some of them are far apart in time from others, so they are children of 'allat, since no single era brings them together, just as children of 'allat are not brought together under one womb. Since 'Isa was close in time to the Prophet ﷺ and there was no prophet between them, they were as if in one time. So he said:

"I am the most deserving of people of 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him." They said: "How, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The prophets are brothers from 'allat." The hadith continues.

There is another explanation, better than this, which is that the Prophet ﷺ likened the religion of the prophets, on which they agreed, namely tawhid, which is worshipping Allah alone without partner, and belief in Him, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the meeting with Him, to one father, because all of them share in it. It is the religion which Allah prescribed for all His prophets. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not become divided therein﴾.

Al-Bukhari, in his Sahih, has a chapter: "Chapter on what has come that the religion of the prophets is one," and he mentioned this hadith. This is the religion of Islam, which Allah informed us is the religion of His prophets and messengers from the first of them, Noah, to the last of them, Muhammad. It is thus like one father. As for the laws of actions and commands, they may differ, and these are like the different mothers, whose offspring came from one father, just as the matter of these differing laws comes from one agreed religion. This is the more correct of the two meanings of the hadith. Nor does the distance between their times require that their times be likened to their mothers and that they be made to have different mothers for that reason. The fact that the mother stands in the position of the law and the father in the position of the religion, the primacy and masculinity of the one, the derivativeness and femininity of the other, and the unity of the father with the plurality of the mothers, all indicate that this is the meaning of the hadith, and Allah knows best.

Reflect on His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Book after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾.

How the agent was omitted here and the verb was put in the passive form, since it occurs in a context of censure of them and negation of knowledge from them.

And since it occurs in a context of mentioning His blessings, His favours and His grace upon them, He said: ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ [Ghafir: 53].

Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 42, verse 15:

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, commanded His Messenger to be just among the sects, saying: ﴿So invite [them to this], and remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Book, and I have been commanded to act justly between you."﴾

So He, glorified is He, commanded him to call to His religion and His Book, to be steadfast himself as he was commanded, not to follow the desires of any of the factions, to believe in the entire truth and not to believe in part of it to the exclusion of the rest, and to be just among the holders of doctrines and religions.

When you reflect on this verse, you find that the people of vain kalam (dialectical theology) and the people of desires and innovation from all the sects are the most deprived of it and the least in their share, while you find that the party of Allah and His Messenger and the helpers of his Sunnah are the most worthy of it and its people.

They, in this matter and others, are happier with the truth than all the sects, for they affirm Allah's power over all existing things, both substances and actions, and His general will. They exalt Him above having in His dominion something He is not able to do, or something that does not fall under His will. They affirm the pre-decreed destiny, and that the servants act according to what Allah has decreed, determined and completed. They affirm that they do not will except what Allah wills, and do not act except after His will, and that whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be. There is no restriction among them in these two matters in any respect.

Destiny, for them, is Allah's power, knowledge, will and creation. Not a single atom moves, or what is more than that, except by His will, knowledge and power. They are truly the believers in "there is no power and no strength except with Allah," while others say it only figuratively, since the world, its upper and lower parts, and every living being performs actions. Its action is by a power in it to act, and it moves from abandoning to acting, from acting to abandoning, and from one act to another, and all of that is by Allah, not by the servant. They believe that whomever Allah guides, none can misguide, and whomever He misguides, none can guide; that He is the one who makes the Muslim a Muslim, the disbeliever a disbeliever, the one who prays a praying person, and the one who moves a moving person; He is the one who makes His servant travel on land and sea, He is the traveler and the servant is the one who travels; He is the mover and the servant is the one who moves; He is the one who causes to stand and the servant is the one who stands; He is the Guide and the servant is the one guided; He is the Feeder and the servant is the one who eats; He is the Giver of life and the Causer of death, and the servant is the one who lives and dies.

Along with this, they affirm the servant's power, will, choice and action in reality, not metaphorically. They agree that the act is other than the thing acted upon, as al-Baghawi and others have related from them.

Their movements and beliefs are actions that belong to them in reality, and they are created by Allah, the Exalted, and made by Him in reality.

What subsists in the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is His knowledge, power, will and bringing into being, and what subsists in them is their action, their acquisition, their movements and their stillnesses.

Thus they are, in reality, the Muslims, the ones who pray, stand and sit. He, glorified is He, is the One who decreed this for them, the One capable of it, who willed it from them, created it for them, and willed and did it after His will. They do not will except what Allah wills, and they do not do except what Allah wills.

And when you weigh this doctrine against the other doctrines, you find it to be the middle path and the straight way.

You find the other doctrines as lines to its right and to its left, some near to it, some far, and some in between.

And if you give al-Fatihah its due, you find it from beginning to end proclaiming this, indicating it, and explicitly stating it, although its praise does not require anything other than this; likewise the perfection of His lordship over the worlds does not require anything other than this. How, then, can all praise belong to One who is not able to do what the inhabitants of His heavens and earth, from angels, jinn, humans, birds and beasts, are able to do; rather, they do what He is not able to do and does not will, and He wills what they do not do, so many of them, He wills what does not come to be and what comes to be He does not will? Does this require the perfection of His praise, and does it require the perfection of His lordship?

(Benefit)

A Shi'i cited the words of Allah Most High, ﴿Say, I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, as proof for a bequest (wasiyyah) in favour of the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt).

It was answered: this is an instruction to honour them, not a bequest to hand over authority to them. So it is evidence against the view of the Shi'a, for if the matter of leadership had been theirs, He would have appointed them to it, not merely enjoined concern for them.

A parallel to this argument is the claim that authority lies with Quraysh and not with the Ansar, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ):

"I enjoin you to treat the Ansar well."

Thus it is understood that authority lies with others.

I say: all of this is a departure from the meaning of the verse and from what it intends, and there is no indication in it for either of the two groups.

The meaning of the verse is: "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you, for there was no clan of Quraysh except that the Prophet (ﷺ) had kinship with it." So he said: I do not ask you for a reward for conveying the message, but maintain the ties of kinship between me and you. And this maintaining of ties is not a reward.

Thus the exception is disjunctive (munqati'), for maintaining kinship is among the obligations of the bond of blood, and it is obligatory upon every person.

This is the exegesis of Ibn 'Abbas, which al-Bukhari transmitted from him in his Sahih.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 42, verse 24:

There are two opinions regarding the meaning of the verse.

The first is the opinion of Mujahid and Muqatil: "If Allah willed, He would seal your heart" means that He would strengthen your heart with patience in bearing their harm, so that it would not be difficult for you.

The second is the opinion of Qatadah: "If Allah willed, He would cause you to forget the Qur'an and cut off the revelation from you."

This second opinion is weaker than the first, for several reasons.

The first reason is that this verse came as a reply to them and a refutation of their statement that Muhammad had lied against Allah and invented this Qur'an. So He answered them with the best answer, which is that Allah the Exalted is capable, and nothing can overpower Him. Had it been as you say, He would have sealed his heart, and he would not be able to bring anything of it at all; rather, the heart would become like a thing sealed up, so that one could not reach what is in it. The meaning would then return to: if he had invented it against Me, I would not have enabled him to do so, and I would not have allowed it to stand.

It is well known that such speech does not issue from a heart that has been sealed. For it contains the knowledge of the earlier and later generations, the knowledge of the beginning and the return, of this world and the Hereafter, the knowledge that none knows except Allah, complete clarity, eloquence, excellence, sublimity, and reports of the unseen, which whoever had his heart sealed could not bring, nor any part of it. So had I not sent it down upon his heart and made it easy upon his tongue, he could not have brought you anything of it.

How, then, does this relate to the meaning mentioned by the others? How does it fit with the narration of their statement? And how does it contain a refutation of them?

The second reason is that merely strengthening the heart with patience in bearing their harm occurs both from the one who is right and from the one who is wrong. Therefore it does not indicate a distinction between them, and it contains no refutation of their statement, for patience in bearing the harm of one who denies does not by itself prove the truthfulness of the one who informs.

The third reason is that one who strengthens the heart of a servant is not called one who seals his heart, and this is not known in the usage of the addressees, nor in the Arabic language, nor is it the established usage in the Qur'an. Rather, the established usage is that sealing upon the heart is applied to the disbelievers in all the occurrences of this expression in the Qur'an, such as His saying, ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾, and His saying, ﴿Have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has sealed upon his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering?﴾, and their like.

(Benefit)

The source of whatever good and evil, and of the praiseworthy and blameworthy qualities, found in the servant comes from the attribute of the Giver and the Withholder. He, glory be to Him, directs His servants between the requirements of these two names. So the portion of the truthful servant from his servanthood through them is gratitude at the time of giving, and dependence (on Allah) at the time of withholding.

He, glory be to Him, gives to him so that he may be grateful to Him, and withholds from him so that he may be needy of Him, so he never ceases to be grateful and needy.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 42, verse 30:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Indeed, for a good deed there is light in the heart, radiance in the face, strength in the body, increase in provision, and love in the hearts of creation. And indeed, for an evil deed there is blackness in the face, darkness in the heart, weakness in the body, decrease in provision, and hatred in the hearts of creation. This is known to the one possessed of insight (ṣāḥib al-baṣīrah), and he witnesses it from himself and from others.

No state of hardship ever befalls a servant except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is greater. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.﴾

And He said to the best of His creation and the companions of His Prophet: ﴿Why is it that when a calamity strikes you, although you had struck (the enemy) with twice as much, you say, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 165].

(Benefit)

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾

In this there is both glad tidings and warning, for He informs us that the calamities of this world are punishments for our sins. He is too merciful to repeat the punishment upon His servant for a sin for which He has already punished him in this world, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is afflicted with any of these filthy things and Allah conceals it, his matter is with Allah: if He wills He punishes him, and if He wills He forgives him. And whoever is punished for it in this world, Allah is too generous to repeat the punishment upon His servant."

And in the hadith: "The prescribed penalties (ḥudūd) are expiations for their people." In the Two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the hadith of ʿUbadah: "Whoever commits some of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him." And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, from him (ﷺ): "No fatigue, nor illness, nor worry, nor grief, nor harm befalls the believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it."

And he said: "Trial does not cease to afflict the believer in his family, his wealth, and his children until he meets Allah with no sin upon him."

In another hadith: "When the believer falls ill, he comes out (of it) like a pure white cloth in its cleanness and color."

In another hadith: "Fever removes sins as the furnace removes the impurity from iron."

In another hadith: "Do not revile fever, for it removes the sins of the children of Adam."

And he said in (Ṭarīq al-Hijratayn):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾

This is general for every calamity, small or great, and witnessing this cause occupies him with seeking forgiveness, which is the greatest of the means for removing that calamity.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: No affliction descends except because of a sin, and no affliction is lifted except by repentance.

The commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 42, verse 39:

Thus He praised them for their strength in defending themselves and for seeking their rights from their souls, until, when they were able to overcome one who had wronged them and to take what was owed to them from him, He urged them toward the noble character of pardon and forgiveness. He said: ﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God. Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers.﴾

He mentioned the three stations: justice, which He permitted; grace, to which He urged; and wrongdoing, which He forbade.

If it is said: how can He praise them for both defending themselves and pardoning, when the two are contradictory?

It is answered: He did not praise them for retaliation and vengeance. He praised them for *intisar* (defending oneself), which is the ability and strength to take back their right. When they were able, He urged them to pardon.

Some of the *salaf* (early generation of Muslims) said regarding this verse: "They used to dislike being humiliated, so when they had power, they pardoned." Thus He praised them for pardon after power, not for the pardon of humiliation, weakness and abasement. This is the perfection by which God praised Himself in His saying: ﴿God is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, and ﴿God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

There is a well-known report: "The bearers of the Throne are four. Two of them say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You; to You belongs praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge.' And two say: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You; to You belongs praise for Your pardon after Your power.'"

For this reason the Messiah, upon whom be blessings and peace, said: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

That is: if You forgive them, You forgive out of might, which is the perfection of power, and out of wisdom, which is the perfection of knowledge. So You forgive after You knew what they did, and Your power encompassed them. A created being may forgive out of inability to retaliate and ignorance of the reality of what the offender did. Pardon from a created being outwardly appears as submission and humiliation, but inwardly it is honor and dignity.

Retaliation outwardly appears as honor, but inwardly it is humiliation. God did not increase anyone in honor through pardon, and no one avenged himself except that this was the case, even if it was only by losing the honor of pardon.

For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) never avenged himself at all.

Reflect on His saying: ﴿they defend themselves﴾. How it indicates that they have a strength by which they are the ones who defend themselves, not that others defend them.

Since defending oneself is a matter in which souls usually do not stop at the limit of justice, but must exceed it, God prescribed equivalence and equality, forbade excess, and urged pardon.

The point is that pardon is one of the characteristics of the *nafs mutma'innah* (the soul at peace), while humiliation is one of the characteristics of the *nafs ammarah* (the soul that commands evil). The essence of the matter is that retaliation is one thing and defending oneself is another. Defending oneself means defending the right of God and for His sake.

Only one who has freed himself from the humiliation of his own portion and from the enslavement of his desire can bear this. Such a person then attains a share of the honor that God allotted to the believers. When someone wrongs him, he defends himself against the aggressor for the sake of God's honor, which God bestowed upon him. Out of zeal for that honor, he refuses to be oppressed or subdued, and out of zeal for the servant who is attributed to the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, he refuses to be humiliated. He says to the one who wronged him: "I am the property of One who does not humiliate His property, and it is not right that anyone should humiliate me."

When his commanding soul remains on its foundations, after he seeks justice, he loves nothing but retaliation and defending his own portion. He delights in overcoming the aggressor, gloating over him and humiliating him.

As for the soul that has come out of the humiliation of its portion and the enslavement of its desire, and has turned to the honor of its monotheism and its return to its Lord, when wrong befalls it, it rises to defend itself out of zeal and in support of the honor by which God has honored it and which it has obtained from Him. In reality this is zeal for its Lord and its Master.

He has given an example of this with two slaves among the slaves who work for produce, who were both farm laborers who were beaten.

One of them, who was struck by his companion, pardoned the one who struck him, out of sincere advice to his master and compassion for the striker, lest the master punish him. He did not burden his master with dismissing him or corrupting him by beating him. So the master thanked the one who pardoned for his pardon, and this was well received.

The other slave, whom his master had placed before him, had adorned and dressed in garments in which he stood before him. Some of the horse-grooms and their like deliberately smeared those garments with dung or tore them. If he had pardoned the one who did this to him, his pardon would not have agreed with his master's opinion or his love. Defending himself would have been more beloved to the master and more suitable. It is as if he says: "He only did this to you out of audacity toward me and contempt for my authority. So when I enable you to punish him, and you humble and subdue him, and do not stop short of seizing him, he is humbled and his heart is broken." Then his master loves that he should not pardon him for a moment, and that he should take from him the master's right. So his defense in that case is purely for the right of his master, not for himself.

Likewise, it is reported from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he passed by a man who sought his help and said: "This man has withheld my right and has not given it to me." Ali said: "Give him his right." When they had passed on, the wrongdoer became obstinate and slapped the one who had the right. The man sought Ali's help again, and Ali turned back and said: "Is that the help?" Then he said to him: "Retaliate against him." The man said: "I have pardoned you, O Commander of the Faithful." So Ali struck the slapper nine lashes and said: "The one you slapped has pardoned you."

This is the right of the ruler. Ali punished him because he had dared against the authority of God, and he did not leave him alone.

A similar case is the story of the man who came to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and said: "Carry me, for by God I am stronger than you and your son al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba." Abu Bakr rolled up his sleeve and struck the man's nose with it, and blood flowed. The man's people came to Abu Bakr and said: "Demand retaliation for us against al-Mughira." He said: "Shall I demand retaliation for you from the guardians of God? I will not demand retaliation for you from him."

Abu Bakr saw that this was a defense by al-Mughira and zeal for God, and for the honor with which God honored the Caliph of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so that by that honor he could carry out his caliphate well and establish his religion. So he gave up retaliation against him, because he had dared against the honor and authority of God, by which He honored His Messenger, his religion and his caliph. This is one kind. And striking out of zeal for the commanding soul is another kind.

Contemplate His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We let mankind taste mercy from Us, they rejoice in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then indeed mankind is ungrateful﴾.

How did He introduce the attaching of mercy, whose reaching them from Allah is certain, with (idha, "when"), while He introduced the befalling of evil with (in, "if")? This is because what Allah pardons is greater in number.

He used the past tense verb, which indicates the certainty of occurrence, for mercy, and the future tense for the occurrence of evil, which indicates that it is not certain, and must be so. And how did He use, for the arrival of mercy, the verb of "tasting" (idhaqah), which indicates that mercy directly touches them and that it is tasted by them? Tasting is the most specific and the most intense kind of contact.

And how did He use, for mercy, the preposition of the starting point (min) with its object attached to Him, saying: ﴿min-na rahmah﴾ ("from Us, mercy")?

For evil, He used the causal preposition (bi, "because of") attached to "what their hands have earned" (kasb aydihim).

And how did He emphasize the first clause, which contains the tasting of mercy, with the particle (inna, "indeed"), but not the second clause?

The secrets of the Noble Qur'an are far more numerous and greater than human minds can encompass.

(Section: On the disapproval of resenting daughters)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female children upon whom He wills, and He bestows male children upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing, Competent.﴾

So He, glorified is He, divided the condition of the spouses into four categories that encompass existence, and He informed that what He has decreed between them of offspring, He has bestowed upon them.

It is sufficient for a servant to expose himself to His wrath that he resents what He has bestowed.

He, glorified is He, began with mention of the females. It was said: to console them, because parents find them burdensome given their station.

It was also said, and this is the better view: He placed them first because the context of the speech is that He does what He wills, not what the parents will. The parents, for the most part, desire only males, while He, glorified is He, has informed that He creates what He wills. So He began with mention of the category that He wills, which the parents do not desire.

I have another view, which is that He, glorified is He, placed first what the Jahiliyyah used to postpone regarding daughters, to the point that they would bury them alive. That is, this category which you postpone is placed first by Me in mention. Consider how He made the females indefinite and defined the males. He compensated for the deficiency of femaleness by placing them first, and compensated for the deficiency of being placed later by defining them, for definiteness is an honouring. It is as if He said: "and He bestows upon whom He wills the famous, well-known males, who are not hidden from you." Then, when He mentioned the two categories together, He placed the males first, giving each of the two sexes its right of precedence and postponement. And Allah knows best what He intended by that.

The point is that resenting females is among the traits of the Jahiliyyah, whom Allah the Exalted censured in His saying: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes darkened, and he suppresses grief. He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given good news of. Should he keep it despite humiliation, or bury it in the dust? Unquestionably, evil is what they judge.﴾ [al-Nahl: 58–59]

And He said: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes darkened, and he suppresses grief.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 17]

From here, some interpreters of dreams interpreted for a man who said to him, "I saw as if my face was black." He said, "Do you have a pregnant wife?" He said, "Yes." He said, "She will give birth to a female for you."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever supports two girls until they reach maturity, he will come on the Day of Resurrection, he and I, like this," and he joined his two fingers.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀ'isha, who said: A woman came to me with two daughters of hers, asking me, and she found with me nothing but one date, so I gave it to her. She took it and split it between her two daughters and did not eat any of it. Then she got up, and she and her daughters left. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon the aftermath of that, and she related to him her story. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever is tested with anything of these daughters and treats them well, they will be a veil for him from the Fire."

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, from ʿUrwa.

It is in the Sahih, and the hadith is in the Musnad of Ahmad.

Also in it, from the hadith of Ayyub ibn Bashir al-Ansari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"No one has three daughters or three sisters, or two daughters or two sisters, and fears Allah regarding them and treats them well, except that he enters Paradise."

Al-Humaydi narrated it from Sufyan, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Ayyub ibn Bashir, from Sa'id al-A'sha, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ):

"Whoever has three daughters or sisters, or two daughters or two sisters, and treats their company well, is patient with them, and fears Allah regarding them, enters Paradise."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ansari said, from Ibn Jurayj: Abu al-Zubayr told me, from ʿUmar ibn Nabhan, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever has three daughters, and is patient with their hardships and their adversities, enters Paradise."

In another narration: "A man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and two?' He said, 'And two.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and one?' He said, 'And one.'"

Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, al-Asamm narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Mukram narrated to us, ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar informed us, al-Nahhas narrated to us, from Shaddad Abu ʿAmmar, from ʿAwf ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever has three daughters, and spends on them until they mature or die, they will be a screen for him from the Fire."

ʿAli ibn al-Madini said: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, al-Nahhas ibn Qahm narrated to us, Shaddad Abu ʿAmmar narrated to us, from ʿAwf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"There is no servant who has three daughters, and spends on them until they mature or die, except that they will be a screen for him from the Fire."

A woman said, "O Messenger of Allah, and two daughters?" He said, "And two daughters."

He said: Abu ʿAmmar also said, from ʿAwf ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I and a woman with dark cheeks are like these two in Paradise," and he gestured with his two fingers.

Fitr ibn Khalifa narrated from Shurahbil ibn Saʿd, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"No Muslim has two daughters, and treats them well as long as they are in his company, and they are in his company, except that they will cause him to enter Paradise."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever has three daughters or sisters, and restrains them, shelters them, and marries them off, enters Paradise." They said, "And two?" He said, "And two," until we thought that if they had said, "And one?" he would have said, "And one."

This is a mursal report.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Harmala ibn ʿImran, who said: I heard Abu ʿUthmana say: I heard ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir al-Juhani say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:

"Whoever has three daughters, and is patient with them, feeds them, gives them drink, and clothes them from his wealth, they will be a screen for him from the Fire."

Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad.

Allah the Exalted has said regarding women: ﴿And if you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something while Allah has placed in it much good.﴾ [al-Nisa': 19]

Likewise, daughters too may bring the servant good in this world and the Hereafter.

And it suffices, in the ugliness of disliking them, that one dislikes what Allah has approved and given to His servant. Salih ibn Ahmad said: My father, when a daughter was born to him, would say: "The Prophets were fathers of daughters," and he would say: "Indeed, what has come concerning daughters is what you know."

Ya'qub ibn Bakhtan said: Seven daughters were born to me, and whenever a daughter was born to me I would enter upon Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and he would say to me, "O Abu Yusuf, the Prophets were fathers of daughters." So his saying would dispel my worry.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever supports two girls until they reach maturity, he will come on the Day of Resurrection, he and I, like this," and he joined his two fingers.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀ'isha, who said: A woman came to me with two daughters of hers, asking me, and she found with me nothing but one date, so I gave it to her. She took it and split it between her two daughters and did not eat any of it. Then she got up, and she and her daughters left. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon the aftermath of that, and she related to him her story. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever is tested with anything of these daughters and treats them well, they will be a veil for him from the Fire."

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, from ʿUrwa.

It is in the Sahih, and the hadith is in the Musnad of Ahmad.

Also in it, from the hadith of Ayyub ibn Bashir al-Ansari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"No one has three daughters or three sisters, or two daughters or two sisters, and fears Allah regarding them and treats them well, except that he enters Paradise."

Al-Humaydi narrated it from Sufyan, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Ayyub ibn Bashir, from Sa'id al-A'sha, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ):

"Whoever has three daughters or sisters, or two daughters or two sisters, and treats their company well, is patient with them, and fears Allah regarding them, enters Paradise."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ansari said, from Ibn Jurayj: Abu al-Zubayr told me, from ʿUmar ibn Nabhan, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever has three daughters, and is patient with their hardships and their adversities, enters Paradise."

In another narration: "A man said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and two?' He said, 'And two.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and one?' He said, 'And one.'"

Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, al-Asamm narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Mukram narrated to us, ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar informed us, al-Nahhas narrated to us, from Shaddad Abu ʿAmmar, from ʿAwf ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever has three daughters, and spends on them until they mature or die, they will be a screen for him from the Fire."

ʿAli ibn al-Madini said: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, al-Nahhas ibn Qahm narrated to us, Shaddad Abu ʿAmmar narrated to us, from ʿAwf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"There is no servant who has three daughters, and spends on them until they mature or die, except that they will be a screen for him from the Fire."

A woman said, "O Messenger of Allah, and two daughters?" He said, "And two daughters."

He said: Abu ʿAmmar also said, from ʿAwf ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I and a woman with dark cheeks are like these two in Paradise," and he gestured with his two fingers.

Fitr ibn Khalifa narrated from Shurahbil ibn Saʿd, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"No Muslim has two daughters, and treats them well as long as they are in his company, and they are in his company, except that they will cause him to enter Paradise."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever has three daughters or sisters, and restrains them, shelters them, and marries them off, enters Paradise." They said, "And two?" He said, "And two," until we thought that if they had said, "And one?" he would have said, "And one."

This is a mursal report.

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Harmala ibn ʿImran, who said: I heard Abu ʿUthmana say: I heard ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir al-Juhani say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:

"Whoever has three daughters, and is patient with them, feeds them, gives them drink, and clothes them from his wealth, they will be a screen for him from the Fire."

Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad.

Allah the Exalted has said regarding women: ﴿And if you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something while Allah has placed in it much good.﴾ [al-Nisa': 19]

Likewise, daughters too may bring the servant good in this world and the Hereafter.

And it suffices, in the ugliness of disliking them, that one dislikes what Allah has approved and given to His servant. Salih ibn Ahmad said: My father, when a daughter was born to him, would say: "The Prophets were fathers of daughters," and he would say: "Indeed, what has come concerning daughters is what you know."

Ya'qub ibn Bakhtan said: Seven daughters were born to me, and whenever a daughter was born to me I would enter upon Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and he would say to me, "O Abu Yusuf, the Prophets were fathers of daughters." So his saying would dispel my worry.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 42, verse 52:

He called His revelation and His command a "spirit" (rūḥ), because life of the hearts and souls is attained through it.

He called it a "light" (nūr), because guidance is attained through it, the hearts are illuminated by it, and it distinguishes truth from falsehood.

He combined the "spirit," through which life is attained, and the "light," through which radiance and illumination are attained. He informed us that His Book, which He sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ), contains both matters: it is a spirit by which hearts live, and a light by which they are illuminated and shine.

He said in *Madarij al-Salikin* (The Stages of the Wayfarers):

He made it a "spirit" because of the life of the hearts and souls that is attained through it.

And a "light" because of the guidance and right direction that is attained through it.

He said in *Ighathat al-Lahfan* (The Rescue of the Distressed):

Allah, glorified is He, only raises those who are raised by the Book and faith, and lowers those who are lowered by their absence.

(Section)

Scholars have differed about the pronoun in His words, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿But We made it a light﴾.

It was said: it refers to the Book.

It was said: it refers to faith.

The correct view is that it refers to the "spirit" mentioned in His words: ﴿a spirit from Our command﴾. Thus He informed us that He made His command a spirit, a light and a guidance. For this reason you see that the one who follows the command and the Sunnah is clothed in the spirit and the light, and in what accompanies them of sweetness, awe, majesty and acceptance, which others are deprived of. As al-Hasan said: "Indeed the believer is the one who is granted sweetness and awe."

He said in *al-Wabil al-Sayyib* (The Heavy Rain):

The correct view is that it refers back to the "spirit," meaning: We made what We revealed to you a light. He called it a spirit because of the good life, knowledge and strength that are attained through it.

He made it a light because of the radiance and illumination that are attained through it, and these two are inseparable. Wherever this life is found through this spirit, illumination and brightness are found, and wherever brightness and illumination are found, life is found.

Whoever his heart does not accept this spirit is dead and in darkness, just as whoever his body is separated from the spirit of life is perished and dissolved.

For this reason, may He be glorified and exalted, struck the two examples of water and fire: the life attained through water, and the radiance and light attained through fire, as He struck these examples at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

He said in *Ijtima' al-Juyush al-Islamiyya* (The Gathering of the Islamic Armies):

Scholars have differed about what the pronoun in His words, exalted is He, ﴿But We made it a light﴾ refers to.

It was said: it refers to faith, because it is the closer of the two mentioned.

It was said: it refers to the Book, for it is the light by which He guides His servants. Our teacher (Ibn Taymiyya) said: the correct view is that it refers back to the "spirit" mentioned in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light, by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. That is, We made that spirit a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. He called His revelation a "spirit" because of the life of the hearts and souls that is attained through it, which is life in reality. Whoever lacks it is dead, not living. Eternal everlasting life in the Abode of Bliss is the fruit of the life of the heart through this spirit which He revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ). Whoever does not live by it in this world is among those for whom is Hell, where he neither dies nor lives. The people with the greatest life in the three abodes, the abode of this world, the abode of the barzakh (intermediate state), and the abode of recompense, are those who have the greatest share of this life through this spirit.

He called it a "spirit" in more than one place in the Qur'an, such as His words: ﴿Raised in degrees, Lord of the Throne, He sends down the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that he may warn of the Day of Meeting﴾ [Ghafir: 15].

And He said: ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying]: "Warn that there is no god but Me, so fear Me"﴾ [al-Nahl: 2].

He called it a "light" because of the enlightenment and illumination of the hearts that is attained through it, and because the spirit is complete with these two attributes: life and light. There is no way to attain them except at the hands of the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, by being guided by what they were sent with, and by receiving beneficial knowledge and righteous action from their niche (of prophethood). Otherwise, the spirit is dead and dark. Even if the servant is pointed out for asceticism, jurisprudence, virtue, theology and research, the life and enlightenment through the spirit that Allah, exalted is He, revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) and made a light by which He guides whom He wills of His servants, lies beyond all of that. Knowledge is not the abundance of transmission, research and speech, but a light by which one distinguishes sound sayings from unsound ones, and truth from falsehood, and what comes from the niche of prophethood from what comes from the opinions of men. It distinguishes the genuine currency bearing the stamp of the Prophet's city, the only currency with which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, accepts a price for His Paradise, from the currency bearing the stamp of Jinkizkhan and his deputies among the philosophers, the Jahmiyya, the Mu'tazila, and everyone who makes for himself a stamp, a mint and a currency that he circulates among the people. All these currencies are counterfeit. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, accepts none of them as the price of His Paradise. Rather, they are returned to their owner when he needs them most, and they become among the deeds which Allah, exalted is He, has come upon and made into scattered dust. For their owner there is a full share of His words: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 103].

This is the state of the people of deeds that were for other than Allah, mighty and majestic is He, or not according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the state of the people of knowledge and speculation who did not receive them from the niche of prophethood, but received them from the refuse of men's minds and the sweepings of their thoughts. They followed their own powers, thoughts and minds in establishing the opinions of men or defending them, understanding what they said and spreading it in gatherings and assemblies, and they turned away from what the Messenger brought, neglecting it entirely. Whoever among them still has a spark of life gives it little attention, seeking virtue.

(Section)

Allah perfected for him (ﷺ) several stages of revelation:

The first: true dreams, which were the beginning of his revelation (ﷺ). He never saw a dream except that it came like the break of dawn.

The second: what the angel would cast into his heart and inner mind without his seeing him, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the Holy Spirit breathed into my heart that no soul will die until it has completed its provision. So fear Allah and seek provision graciously, and let the delay of provision not lead you to seek it through disobedience to Allah, for what is with Allah is not attained except through obedience to Him."

The third: that the angel would appear to him as a man and address him until he understood what he was saying. In this stage, the Companions sometimes saw him.

The fourth: that revelation would come to him like the ringing of a bell, and this was the hardest on him. The angel would overwhelm him, so that his forehead would drip with sweat on a very cold day, and his mount would kneel down with him to the ground if he was riding it. Revelation once came to him in this way while his thigh was upon the thigh of Zayd ibn Thabit, and it became so heavy on him that it nearly crushed it.

The fifth: that he would see the angel in his original form, and he would reveal to him what Allah willed to reveal. This happened to him twice, as Allah mentioned in [al-Najm: 7, 13].

The sixth: what Allah revealed to him while he was above the heavens on the night of the Ascension (al-Mi'raj), including the obligation of prayer and other things.

The seventh: Allah's speech to him, from Him to him, without an intermediary angel, as Allah spoke to Musa ibn Imran. This stage is certainly established for Musa by the explicit text of the Qur'an, and its establishment for our Prophet (ﷺ) is in the hadith of the Isra' (Night Journey).

Some have added an eighth stage, which is Allah speaking to him face to face without a veil. This is according to the view of those who say that he (ﷺ) saw his Lord, blessed and exalted is He. It is a matter of disagreement between the early generations (salaf) and later generations (khalaf). Yet the majority of the Companions, indeed all of them, along with Aisha, held the view, as Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi reported, that it was a consensus (ijma') of the Companions.
